LESSON: BIBLE PATRIARCHS ABRAHAM

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Holy Bible
Topic 2.6: Bible Patriarchs Abraham

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Bible Patriarchs Abraham. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why was the name Abram changed?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life
2. discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham
3. appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BIBLE PATRIARCHS ABRAHAM
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Bible Patriarchs Abraham helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BIBLE PATRIARCHS ABRAHAM
Study Bible Patriarchs Abraham like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life

What this means
In this part you learn to obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Bible Patriarchs Abraham” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham

What this means
In this part you learn to discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible Patriarchs Abraham in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Bible Patriarchs Abraham is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Bible Patriarchs Abraham” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Bible Patriarchs Abraham in your own words. (skill: discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Bible Patriarchs Abraham to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life.
3. Practise this skill: discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate God’s blessings in his or her life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Bible Patriarchs Abraham from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Bible Patriarchs Abraham: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Bible Patriarchs Abraham?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why was the name Abram changed?
2. How did Abraham show obedience to God?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Bible Patriarchs Abraham means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: obey God’s instructions in his or her day-to-day life.
5. Be able to: discuss Abram’s change of name to Abraham.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
